# c09 — SUYU-GURecomp facts vs. MHGU 1.4.0 disassembly

Source: SUYU-GURecomp commit 35015f1, `game_settings.cpp` lines 1208/1218 (address constants around the 0x139E8xx message-iteration code and the motion-blur render pass). Address convention: SUYU "main+X" equals our vaddr X.

| vaddr | meaning | SUYU cite | status | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x139e800 | Interior code address, **not** a function entry: this is the virtual-call tail of the routine that returns at 0x139e820. `this` is already in r4 (not set up here), one argument is passed in r6, the method pointer is fetched from vtable slot 60 (0x3C) and invoked; SUYU pairs this address with 0x139e814, i.e. the very instruction after that call, so the literal pair reads as a 20-byte code range / call-site descriptor, not as two entry points | game_settings.cpp:1208 | VERIFIED | `0139e808: ldr r2, [r0, #60]` + `0139e810: blx r2` — an indirect vtable dispatch that uses callee-saved r4/r6 without any prologue, so 0x139e800 can only be mid-function |
| 0x139e814 | Interior code address, **not** a function entry: the decision/exit block of the same routine. It compares the virtual call's return value against 1 (success/true); on mismatch it branches back into the loop body at 0x139e664, on match it falls straight into the epilogue that releases the 132-byte frame and returns — so the enclosing function ends at 0x139e820 and everything from 0x139e824 on (`.word 0x004a2a44`, 0x004a94dc, 0x004a94c4, 0x004a9d40, 0x004a9f04) is a literal pool, followed at 0x139e838 by a separate 2-instruction stub that just returns 0 | game_settings.cpp:1208 | VERIFIED | `0139e814: cmp r0, #1` + `0139e81c: add sp, sp, #132` / `0139e820: pop {r4, r5, r6, r7, r8, r9, r10, r11, pc}` — result test immediately followed by the function's own frame teardown, i.e. inside the function, not at its start |
| 0x8bcd84 | Entry point of the motion-blur render routine (SUYU's `kMotionBlurRender`). Real function prologue: saves all callee-saved GPRs, sets up a frame pointer, re-aligns sp, saves the VFP callee-saved doubles `d8-d15` (the `coproc`-decoded `.word 0xed2d8b10`), then carves a 552-byte local frame; afterwards it caches the incoming args (`mov r4, r1` / `mov r5, r0`) and starts with a two-level null check on `[r4+480]` → `[+640]` that early-outs to 0x8c009c, then reads more fields `[+548]` and `[r5+60]` | game_settings.cpp:1218 | VERIFIED | `008bcd84: push {r4, r5, r6, r7, r8, r9, r10, r11, lr}` + `008bcd94: sub sp, sp, #552` — textbook AAPCS prologue with a large frame, i.e. a genuine function entry, not interior code |
